description:
memory.rs:133-138:

    fn current_state(&self, type_name: &'static str, account_id: &str) -> u64 {
        *self
            .states
            .get(&(type_name, account_id.to_owned()))
            .unwrap_or(&0)
    }

The `.unwrap_or(&0)` returns &u64, then `*` deref. The idiomatic Rust form for Option<&Copy> is:

    self.states.get(...).copied().unwrap_or(0)

…or, since Option::copied exists since Rust 1.35, this is just standard. The `&0` is a clippy-flagged taste violation (option_as_ref_deref / unnecessary_lazy_evaluations adjacent).

Same pattern at line 422 with `unwrap_or(&[])`:

    let log = inner.change_log.get(&(...))
        .map(Vec::as_slice)
        .unwrap_or(&[]);

…is fine because Vec::as_slice returns &[], not &&[]. The Option<&Vec<_>> → Option<&[_]> via .map(Vec::as_slice) is idiomatic. Only line 134 is non-idiomatic.

Engineering cost: trivial. Flagged as idiomatic-rust,clippy. Not a bug, but a `.copied()` makes the intent ("read a u64") visible in the call chain.
title: Inner::current_state uses *self.states.get().unwrap_or(&0) instead of .copied().unwrap_or(0)
